notes.text: Peter laid all things before them — So he did not take it ill to be questioned, nor desire to be treated as infallible. And he answers the more mildly because it related to a point which he had not readily believed himself.
Being in a trance — Which suspends the use of the outward senses.
Saved — With the full Christian salvation, in this world and the world to come.

To us, when we believed — The sense is, because we believed, not because we were circumcised, was the Holy Ghost given to us. What was I - A mere instrument in God's hand. They had inquired only concerning his eating with the Gentiles. He satisfies them likewise concerning his baptizing them, and shows that he had done right in going to Cornelius, not only by the command of God, but also by the event, the descent of the Holy Ghost. And who are we that we should withstand God? Particularly by laying down rules of Christian communion which exclude any whom he has admitted into the Church of the first born, from worshipping God together. O that all Church governors would consider how bold an usurpation this is on the authority of the supreme Lord of the Church! O that the sin of thus withstanding God may not be laid to the charge of those, who perhaps with a good intention, but in an over fondness for their own forms, have done it, and are continually doing it.
They glorified God — Being thoroughly satisfied. Repentance unto life - True repentance is a change from spiritual death to spiritual life, and leads to life everlasting.

glossa.text: *The fourfooted beasts of the earth,* etc. ((RAB.)) I marvel that some interpret this of meats, etc., *as far as* he set forth the mystery of this vision.

*Therefore to the Gentiles also,* etc. This is that which is read in Job: From the North gold shall come, and to God fearful praise, because the brightness of faith arose first in the cold breast of the Gentiles, and for that same unlooked-for faith Judaea glorifies God with trembling.

notes.text: Heavens of heavens — Ye highest heavens, the place of God's throne. Waters - Ye clouds which are above a part of the heavens.
Established — He hath made them constant and incorruptible, not changeable, as the things of the lower world. A decree - Concerning their continuance.
Dragons — Either serpents, which hide in the deep caverns of the earth; or whales, and other sea-monsters, which dwell in the depths of the sea.

Fire — Lightnings and other fireworks of the air. Vapor - Or, fumes: hot exhalations. Fulfilling his word - Executing his commands, either for the comfort or punishment of the inhabitants of the earth.
Above — Above all the glories which are in earth and in heaven.

The horn — In scripture commonly denotes strength, victory, glory, and felicity. An exhortation to praise God for his love to his people, ver. 1-5. And for enabling them to overcome their enemies, ver. 6- 9.

glossa.text: *Praise ye the Lord from the heavens.* ((CASS.)) By the mention of a few he exhorts the whole creation to praise God. There are certain things which have a spirit of praising God in that affection wherewith God pleases them: certain have no understanding, but because they themselves are good in their own order, and are referred to the beauty of the whole, they praise not of themselves, but by them God is praised through those that consider them: and so after a sort they praise, because from them the praise of God is born in us, whereto the prophet here admonishes us.

*For he spoke, and they were made.* ((CASS.)) This against those who say that the world is coeternal with God; there follows: *He commanded.* By his word, and they were created. First he said, *made,* afterward *created.* For make we also can, but not create. He therefore alone creates, which is proper to the Godhead. Praise from his works

*He hath established.* From his power he is almighty, whose works are not changed.

*Unto the age, and unto the age of the age.* ((CAS.)) And though the heaven be new, yet they are said to be well established by God, which are made new through Christ and remain bettered. And here is praise from his power.

*Praise ye the Lady *Dominam*; read *Dominum*, "the Lord".* The second part, where, the heavenly things being enumerated, he descends to earthly things. Turning therefore to them, as exhorting us that by the consideration of them we may praise God, which things considered lay open the praise of God, he says: O ye that are of the earth. *All ye deeps.* *ubyssi* ((AUG.)) The depth of the waters, etc., *as far as* these therefore, that is, he exhorts us to praise by the consideration of them.

*Which do his word.* This therefore because it seemed to certain men that God ruled the higher things, but despised these lower ones, and that they were ruled by chance; but these also God does, and in these least things he is praised, and alleluia is sung.

*Confession.* ((CAS.)) Above he spoke first of heaven, afterward of earth; here of all together. And he takes by heaven all higher things, and by earth all lower things. ((AUG.)) *His confession above heaven and earth.* All things confess him in themselves or in others; the beauty of all things is the voice of them that confess, in those who consider them, that is, let those who consider praise him, both from earthly and from heavenly things, than which there is nothing better.
*He hath exalted the horn of his people.* ((ID.)) Behold what Aggeus and Zacharias prophesied. Now the horn of his people is lowly in tribulations, but when the Lord shall come, it shall be exalted.

notes.text: And I saw — So it runs, chap. xix, 11, xx, 1, 4, 11, in a succession. All these several representations follow one another in order: so the vision reaches into eternity. A new heaven and a new earth - After the resurrection and general judgment. St. John is not now describing a flourishing state of the church, but a new and eternal state of all things. For the first heaven and the first earth - Not only the lowest part of heaven, not only the solar system, but the whole ethereal heaven, with all its host, whether of planets or fixed stars, Isai xxxiv, 4 Matt. xxiv, 29. All the former things will be done away, that all may become new, verses 4, 5, 2 Pet. iii, 10, 12. Are passed away - But in the fourth verse it is said, "are gone away." There the stronger word is used; for death, mourning, and sorrow go away all together: the former heaven and earth only pass away, giving place to the new heaven and the new earth.

And I saw the holy city — The new heaven, the new earth, and the new Jerusalem, are closely connected. This city is wholly new, belonging not to this world, not to the millennium, but to eternity. This appears from the series of the vision, the magnificence of the description, and the opposition of this city to the second death, chap. xx, 11, 12; xxi, 1, 2, 5, 8, 9; xxii, 5. Coming down - In the very act of descending.
They shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God — So shall the covenant between God and his people be executed in the most glorious manner.

And death shall be no more — This is a full proof that this whole description belongs not to time, but eternity. Neither shall sorrow, or crying, or pain, be any more: for the former things are gone away - Under the former heaven, and upon the former earth, there was death and sorrow, crying and pain; all which occasioned many tears: but now pain and sorrow are fled away, and the saints have everlasting life and joy.

And he that sat upon the throne said — Not to St. John only. From the first mention of "him that sat upon the throne," chap. iv, 2, this is the first speech which is expressly ascribed to him. And he - The angel. Saith to me Write - As follows. These sayings are faithful and true - This includes all that went before. The apostle seems again to have ceased writing, being overcome with ecstasy at the voice of him that spake.

And he — That sat upon the throne. Said to me, It is done - All that the prophets had spoken; all that was spoken, chap. iv, 1. We read this expression twice in this prophecy: first, chap. xvi, 17, at the fulfilling of the wrath of God; and here, at the making all things new. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end - The latter explains the former: the Everlasting. I will give to him that thirsteth - The Lamb saith the same, chap. xxii, 17.

glossa.text: *And I saw.* In this seventh vision he treats of the renewing of the elements and the glorification of the saints, describing the merits through which the saints are thus glorified. *A new heaven and a new earth.* The change of the air and of the earth is not doubtful, but that it comes to pass through fire. But concerning water there is doubt, for it is believed to have purgation in itself.

*As a bride adorned.* As a bridegroom sends gifts beforehand to his bride before he leads her home, so does Christ send to the Church faith and virtues and good works before he receives her into glory.

*A great voice from the throne.* When he had said that he had seen the renewing of the elements and the glorification of the saints, this was unknown, and, lest it should seem past believing, he adds the authority of the holy Fathers, who foretold this. *Behold the tabernacle.* That is, it is plain that the humanity of Christ shall be in that same glory in which it warred, and the men who imitated him and used those things well.

 *And they his people.* That is, offending in nothing, which cannot be while they are in mortal flesh.
*And death.* Truly there shall be no tears there, because there shall be no cause of tears.

*And he said.* As if he should say: Write whatsoever has been shown thee concerning this renewing. This was done for the profit of those now present, for whom I have been bidden to write these things. *Write: for these,* etc. Bidding him write, and announce to others, he subjoins an exhortation, that all may labour to belong to this renewing.

*And he said to me.* When the authority of the saints concerning this renewing has been set down, he sets down the authority of God himself. *It is done.* Lest anyone should ask: What shall come to pass after that renewing, it is said to him that nothing remains to be done.

 *Alpha and Omega.* As if he should say: This renewing I shall be able to make, because I created all things, and in me all things shall be consummated. *To him that thirsteth.* I will give, not to him that thirsteth for an hour, but to him that perseveres.

notes.text: Jesus saith — Namely, the next day; on Thursday, in the morning. Here the scene, as it were, is opened, for the discourse which is continued in the following chapters. Now - While I speak this, the Son of man is glorified - Being fully entered into his glorious work of redemption. This evidently relates to the glory which belongs to his suffering in so holy and victorious a manner.
Ye cannot come — Not yet; being not yet ripe for it. John vii, 34.
A new commandment — Not new in itself; but new in the school of Christ: for he had never before taught it them expressly. Likewise new, as to the degree of it, as I have loved you.

glossa.text:
*Little children. ((ID.))* Because he had said that God would quickly glorify him, etc., *as far as* this cannot be taken so, because what follows would not agree.

*Whither I go you cannot come.* The apostles, not yet confirmed in spirit, could not now follow the Lord, that is, die for the Lord and for justice, or come to the immortal life to which he himself was going; but they were to follow afterwards. And how they might be fit and go where he goes before, he teaches.

*A new commandment I give. ((AUG.))* Not that this is not in the old law, *Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself,* etc., *as far as* which love makes a man die to the world.

*That you love one another, as I have loved you.* Let not that love of God be thought passed over which is in the love of the neighbour; for in the neighbour nothing is loved but God, as Christ also loves God in us; and not that we have this, but that we might have it, as a physician in a sick man loves not the disease but the health which he comes to give.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them, “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘These are the living things which you may eat among all the animals that are on the earth. Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat. “‘Nevertheless these you shall not eat of those that chew the cud, or of those who part the hoof: the camel, because he chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, he is […]
echoes.note: The vision's core conflict — a divine command to 'kill and eat' four-footed animals, creeping things, and birds, and Peter's refusal because 'nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth' — directly engages the Levitical taxonomy of clean and unclean creatures. Volume is high (the whole pericope turns on these dietary categories); recurrence is strong (the sister account in Acts 10 and the parallel here); thematic coherence is high. The narrative reads the Levitical food law figurally, the abolition of the clean/unclean boundary dramatizing the inclusion of Gentiles.

echoes.text: Then I said, Ah Lord Yahweh! behold, my soul has not been polluted; for from my youth up even until now have I not eaten of that which dies of itself, or is torn of animals; neither came there abominable flesh into my mouth.
echoes.note: Peter's protest, 'Not so, Lord, for nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth,' closely echoes Ezekiel's own protest at the command to eat defiling food: 'I have not eaten of that which dies of itself... neither came there abominable flesh into my mouth.' The verbal and situational parallel (prophet objecting to a divine eating-command on grounds of lifelong purity) is striking; this is a strong allusion, perhaps the model for Peter's words.

echoes.text: You shall not eat any abominable thing. These are the animals which you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat, the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the chamois. Every animal that parts the hoof, and has the hoof cloven in two and chews the cud, among the animals, that may you eat. Nevertheless these you shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of those who have the hoof cloven: the camel, the hare, and the […]
echoes.note: The Deuteronomic restatement of the clean/unclean animal law stands behind Peter's scruple alongside Leviticus 11. Lower volume than Leviticus (no distinctive verbal pickup unique to Deuteronomy), but the same legal substrate the vision overturns.

echoes.text: Of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every sort into the ship, to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female. Of the birds after their kind, of the livestock after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every sort will come to you, to keep them alive.
echoes.note: The vision's catalogue — 'four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky' — recalls the ordered creaturely classes gathered to the ark (beasts after their kind, creeping things, fowl). The taxonomic phrasing echoes the Genesis flood inventory of all flesh; thematic coherence is moderate (universal scope of living kinds), volume modest.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: Peter's report that 'the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning' frames Gentile Spirit-reception by the same Joel oracle invoked at Pentecost ('I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh'). The 'all flesh' universality of Joel undergirds the argument that the same gift is now given to Gentiles; medium volume, high thematic coherence with the chapter's inclusion theme.

echoes.text: God said, “Let the earth produce living creatures after their kind, livestock, creeping things, and animals of the earth after their kind”; and it was so. God made the animals of the earth after their kind, and the livestock after their kind, and everything that creeps on the ground after its kind. God saw that it was good. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds […]
echoes.note: The triad of earth-beasts, creeping things, and birds also recalls the creation account's enumeration of the living creatures over which humanity is given dominion. A faint echo: the categories are generic and shared with the flood narrative, so attribution to Genesis 1 specifically is weak.

echoes.text: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: The pairing of cleansing ('What God has cleansed, don't you call unclean') with the gift of the Spirit recalls Ezekiel's promise to sprinkle clean water and put a new Spirit within the people. A figural resonance — purification and Spirit-bestowal joined — rather than a verbal borrowing.

echoes.text: Neither let the foreigner, who has joined himself to Yahweh, speak, saying, “Yahweh will surely separate me from his people”; neither let the eunuch say, “Behold, I am a dry tree.” For thus says Yahweh, “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and hold fast my covenant: to them I will give in my house and within my walls a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, […]
echoes.note: Jerusalem's verdict that 'God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life' coheres with Isaiah's vision of foreigners joined to the LORD and gathered to his house. A thematic echo of Gentile incorporation; no verbal link, so confidence is low.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

places.name: Judea
places.id: The Roman administrative province (later procuratorial province) covering the southern hill country of Israel — Jerusalem, the Judean wilderness, and territory south to the Negev. The Greco-Roman successor to the Hasmonean and Herodian Iudaea. Pin sits in the central hill country.

places.name: Joppa
places.id: Tel Yafo (Jaffa) on the Mediterranean coast, the natural harbor for Jerusalem. Listed in Thutmose III's Karnak topographical list and in the Amarna letters.

places.name: Caesarea
places.id: On the Mediterranean coast c. 60 km northwest of Jerusalem, on the site of an earlier Hellenistic Strato's Tower. Rebuilt by Herod the Great as a deepwater harbor with concrete moles, an aqueduct from Mount Carmel, and a temple to Roma and Augustus. The administrative capital of Roman Judea/Palaestina from c. 6 A.D. Distinct from Caesarea Philippi (Banias) at the foot of Mount Hermon.

echoes.text: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
echoes.note: Verbal and thematic core: 'new heavens and a new earth' (LXX ouranos kainos kai ge kaine) with the 'former things not remembered/passed away' motif — John's 'new heaven and a new earth' and 'the first things have passed away' (v.4) draws on both halves. Strongest availability and recurrence; Hays' volume and thematic coherence both high.

echoes.text: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says Yahweh, “so your seed and your name shall remain.
echoes.note: Doublet of 65:17: 'the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me' — reinforces the eschatological permanence theme. Together with 65:17 establishes the dominant intertext.

echoes.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
echoes.note: 'He will wipe away every tear' (v.4) echoes 'the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces' and 'he will swallow up death forever' — joint source for tear-wiping and death's abolition. MT 'swallow up death' vs LXX 'death prevailed having swallowed' diverges; John follows the death-abolished sense (cf. MT / Theodotion). High volume.

echoes.text: My tent also shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
echoes.note: Covenant-dwelling formula: 'My dwelling place (LXX kataskenosis) will be with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people' — directly behind v.3 ('God's dwelling is with people... they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God'). Recurrence with Lev 26 strengthens.

echoes.text: I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you. I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
echoes.note: Foundational covenant formula: 'I will set my tabernacle/dwelling among you... I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be my people.' Source of the Ezek 37:27 reuse; Revelation's plural 'peoples' (laoi, best text) universalizes the singular covenant 'people.'

echoes.text: Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for, behold, I come, and I will dwell in your midst,’ says Yahweh. Many nations shall join themselves to Yahweh in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that Yahweh of Armies has sent me to you.
echoes.note: 'I will dwell in the midst of you... and many nations shall join themselves to the LORD... and shall be my people' — supports v.3's expanded 'peoples' and the God-dwelling-with-humanity theme; verbal contact with the dwelling formula.

echoes.text: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion; put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.
echoes.note: 'Awake, awake... O Jerusalem, the holy city; put on your beautiful garments' — behind the 'holy city' title (v.2) and the adornment imagery; recurs at 21:27 ('nothing unclean shall enter').

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: Bridal-adornment simile (v.2): 'as a bridegroom decks himself... and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels' — close conceptual and verbal match for 'prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.'

echoes.text: For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness go out as brightness, and her salvation as a lamp that burns. The nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of Yahweh shall name. You shall also be a crown of beauty in the hand of Yahweh, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God. You shall no more be termed Forsaken; […]
echoes.note: Zion as bride married to God: 'as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride... so shall your God rejoice over you'; the city given a new name. Supports the New Jerusalem-as-bride identification.

echoes.text: The Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”
echoes.note: 'Sorrow and sighing shall flee away' parallels 'no more mourning, nor crying, nor pain' (v.4); paired with 51:11. Thematic coherence high though verbal contact diffuse.

echoes.text: The ransomed of Yahweh shall return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy shall be on their heads. They shall obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
echoes.note: Doublet of 35:10 ('sorrow and sighing shall flee away'); reinforces the abolition-of-grief catalogue in v.4.

echoes.text: and I will bring them, and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”
echoes.note: 'They shall be my people and I will be their God' — another instance of the covenant formula feeding v.3; faint given many parallel attestations.

echoes.text: I will sow her to me in the earth; and I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; and I will tell those who were not my people, ‘You are my people;’ and they will say, ‘My God!’”
echoes.note: 'I will say... You are my people, and they shall say, You are my God' — covenant-formula reuse; low independent weight beside Lev 26 / Ezek 37.

echoes.text: There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: The 'peoples' (laoi) who serve in the everlasting kingdom may color the plural in v.3; faint and contested.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: 'New heaven and a new earth' as deliberate recreation of the Gen 1 'heavens and the earth' — figural new-creation framing; structurally cued but verbally generic.

echoes.text: “Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old.
echoes.note: 'Remember not the former things' — paired with 43:19 (next pericope); supports 'the first/former things have passed away' (v.4).

echoes.text: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
echoes.note: 'Am I the sea?' / the sea as chaos-monster domain may underlie 'the sea is no more' (v.1); part of the OT chaos-sea / Leviathan complex.

echoes.text: Daniel spoke and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the sky broke out on the great sea. Four great animals came up from the sea, diverse one from another.
echoes.note: The 'great sea' from which the beasts arise — 'the sea is no more' (v.1) as the elimination of the source of chaos/the beast (cf. Rev 13:1). Figural; contested.

echoes.text: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
echoes.note: 'Behold, I am making all things new' (v.5) draws on 'Behold, I am doing a new thing' (idou ego poio kaina, LXX) — the 'behold... new' formula. High verbal contact with the LXX of Isa 43:19.

echoes.text: “Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
echoes.note: 'I will give freely (dorean) to him who is thirsty from the spring of the water of life' (v.6) echoes 'Ho, every one who thirsts, come to the waters... without money' — free gift to the thirsty. Verbal ('thirsty,' 'freely/without price') and thematic match.

echoes.text: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.
echoes.note: 'I am the first, and I am the last' underlies 'the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End' (v.6); recurs at Rev 1:8,17; 22:13. Cf. also Isa 41:4; 48:12 for the same self-predication.

echoes.text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
echoes.note: 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son' — Davidic adoption formula directly behind 'I will be his God, and he will be my son' (v.7). Revelation democratizes the royal promise to every overcomer.

echoes.text: He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation!’ I will also appoint him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
echoes.note: Davidic sonship: 'He shall cry to me, You are my Father, my God... I will make him the firstborn' — reinforces 2 Sam 7:14 behind v.7; royal-firstborn coloring.

echoes.text: “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
echoes.note: 'I am the first, I also am the last' — doublet of 44:6 supporting the Alpha-Omega self-designation (v.6).

echoes.text: It will happen in that day, that living waters will go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea; in summer and in winter will it be.
echoes.note: 'Living waters shall flow out from Jerusalem' supports 'the spring of the water of life' (v.6); fully developed in Rev 22:1. Thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: For with you is the spring of life. In your light shall we see light.
echoes.note: 'With you is the fountain of life' — direct verbal source for 'the spring of the water of life' (v.6); pege zoes in LXX.

echoes.text: Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky.
echoes.note: 'Fire and sulfur (brimstone)' raining on Sodom (v.8 'fire and sulfur') — the canonical brimstone-judgment image. Cf. Ezek 38:22; Ps 11:6.

echoes.text: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
echoes.note: 'The fountain of living waters' (God) contrasted with broken cisterns — colors the 'spring of the water of life' (v.6).

echoes.text: They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them: for he who has mercy on them will lead them, even by springs of water he will guide them.
echoes.note: 'Springs of water will guide them' for the redeemed who 'will not hunger or thirst' — feeds the thirst/spring motif (v.6); also echoed in Rev 7:16-17.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: 'Everyone whose name is written in the book' — undergirds the overcomer/inheritance contrast with the excluded (v.7-8) and the book-of-life of v.27.

echoes.text: With pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
echoes.note: 'Fire and sulfur' rained in judgment on Gog — reinforces the 'lake that burns with fire and sulfur' (v.8).

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: 'Now the Son of Man has been glorified' draws on the one like a son of man who receives glory and dominion. John transposes the apocalyptic enthronement onto the hour of the cross, his signature reading of Daniel's glorification. Volume, recurrence, and coherence across John are maximal.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Love one another' restates 'you shall love your neighbor as yourself,' the OT love command Jesus calls 'new' by christological measure ('as I have loved you'). Availability and recurrence are high; the command is the explicit scriptural substrate of the new commandment. Coherence with the footwashing example is strong.

echoes.text: and he said to me, “You are my servant; Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”
echoes.note: 'You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified' provides the servant-glorification pattern behind 'God has been glorified in him... God will glorify him.' The mutual glorifying of God and his agent coheres with John's Servant Christology. The verbal overlap on 'glorified in' is notable.

echoes.text: Behold, the days come, says Yahweh, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they broke, although I was a husband to them, says Yahweh. But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Yahweh: I will put my law in […]
echoes.note: Calling the love command 'new' evokes the new covenant with the law written on the heart, fitting the Passover/farewell setting. John presents internalized covenant love as the mark of the disciples. The conceptual coherence is strong though the wording is not quoted.

echoes.text: You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
echoes.note: The Shema's 'love the LORD your God' stands behind the love command, here redirected to mutual love as the visible sign of belonging to Jesus. Pairing neighbor-love (Lev 19:18) with covenant love is a standard Second-Temple combination. Echo is conceptual.

echoes.text: I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: The promise of a new heart and spirit enabling obedience underlies the capacity to keep the 'new' commandment of love. The link is thematic to the new-covenant cluster and not verbally explicit. Faint, marked contested.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

registers.label: Spare
lines: Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
A new command: love one another as I have loved you.
By this everyone will know we are his.
See, the home of God is among mortals; he makes all things new.
He will wipe every tear from their eyes.
Sun and moon, sea and mountain, young and old: praise the Lord.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Come as you are, with whatever the week has worn down in you, and hear a voice from the throne: See, I am making all things new.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
The God who flung the stars and named the sea comes close enough to wipe the tears from your face with his own hand.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
And he leaves us one new command to carry out the door: love one another, the way I have loved you.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
For by this love — not by our arguing, not by our certainty — the world will know whose we are.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
So all you works of the Lord, all you peoples, sing the new song:
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A new command: love one another as I have loved you.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
See, God makes a home with us and makes all things new.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He wipes the tears from every face with his own hand.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
All creation, sing; come, let us worship.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
